Spear with a thick wooden (bamboo?) two part shaft, wooden foresahft, and metal point.  The shaft is made of two pieces of wood, joined together by braided fiber rope and an unknown adhesive.  This rope extends, becomes a thick braid, winds around the shaft multiple times, and eventually secures the haft point between the metal point and the foreshaft, serving as lashing.  The end of the shaft into which the foreshaft inserts is wrapped with two strips of woven rattan.  The foreshaft tapers to a point at the proximal end which inserts into the shaft -- the two parts detach.  As mentioned, the join between the foreshaft and point is lashed with thick fiber robe.  The point has a four sided shaft/tang that becomes a large, triangular head with extending barbs at the base.
Curatorial Notes: card indicates that the handle was cut off on account of packing, but it appears to be intact.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large blue and white plate, with simple floral design.  Glassy, cracked, greenish glaze, straight rim. Interior design on wall is chrysanthemum near rim, rim has single ring.  Exterior design is single ring on rim, double one near base.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large, heavy, finely cracked, glassy blue and greenish white deep plate, flaring rim.  Swatow-type.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Fragment, sherds, large, greenish blue and white plate, uncracked, straight rim, glassy glaze, simple design.  Swatow-type.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Fragment, sherds, blue and chalky white large plate, with slightly flaring rim, crude design, uncracked.  Swatow-type.  Later note:  Large blue and white plate with flaring rim.  Base and footring completely glazed, very sandy, both sides of ring slant to rounded edge, exterior side is deeper.  Body is fine greyish white porcelain.  Glaze is quite white, semi-glassy, finely pitted, somewhat crackled.  Blue is soft pale blue, somewhat greyish.  Interior design in bottom is too fragmentary to describe, surrounded by a double ring, flaring rim has design, surrounded by double rings.  Exterior design is single line below rim, knot-like design on wall, single line near base.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Fragment, arge crudely figured blue and white bowl, with flaring rim, with crosshatch design on it.  Glassy, uncracked.  Swatow-type.  Later note:  Body is hard, grey stoneware.  Glaze is medium thickness, glassy, greenish, and has many imperfections.  Design is a large, flower in bottom enclosed in wave border.  Rim has trellis design.  Outside wall has flower decoration.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, large, cracked shallow blue and greenish white bowl, badly mottled.  Simple floral elements and straight rim.  Swatow-type.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large, crackled, shallow blue and greyish white bowl, badly mottled.  Simple floral elements and straight rim.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, large, heavy blue and greenish white cracked bowl, with flaring rim carrying design.  Floral design on bottom and exterior.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Miscellaneous bowl sherds, which belong to large bowls very similar to B4-88.  Swatow-type.  Later note:  Body is tannish white stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, crackled, light green.  Blue ranges from pale blue to black to a true royal blue to navy.  Interior designs include double rings enclose cross-hatch and dot motif.  Exterior designs include single line below rim, large spiral-centered flowers with curving leaves and stems.  One sherd has pale blue single line and curving leaves.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Fragment, sherds, small blue and white bowl - plain on interior, with elaborate deep blue design on exterior.  Flaring rim, glassy, uncrackled.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Fragment, sherds, blue and white shallow bowl, glassy, uncrackled.  Fluted exterior, crude floral design on interior.  Flaring rim.  Later note:  Large blue and white plate with flaring rim, lower wall fluted.  Body is greyish porcelain.  Glaze is glassy, greyish white.  Blue is soft greyish blue to black.  Interior design is large chrysanthemums on upper wall, flaring rim has cross-hatch and dot motif.  Exterior is fluted wall.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Major fragment, small blue and greenish white bowl, with unglazed ring in bottom.  Glassy, cracked.  Straight rim, only a pair of enclosing lines on interior and exterior.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white bowl.  Major base fragment, sherd, grey blue and cream white bowl, with crude late design.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Later note:  Small blue and white bowl.  Base and footring unglazed, slightly curving sides, flat base, chattermarks very visible on base.  Body is somewhat coarse, white stoneware, tan where unglazed.  Glaze is slightly glassy, finely crackled, grey.  Blue is very light, greyish.  Interior design is parabola in bottom, surrounded by unglazed ring, double concentric ring enclosed unglazed ring.  Exterior design is paneled design on walls, looks like a deteriorated versions of C43-2 and C1-44.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Rim fragment, sherds, blue and white deep plate with flaring rim.  Glassy, cracked.  Blotchy design on rim only.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, crude blue and greenish white plate, with simple, rough design.  Heavily cracked.  Swatow-type platter, and a large blue and white Swatow-type plate.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Fragment, sherds, blue and greenish white shallow bowl, with flaring rim.  Heavily crackled.  Exterior fluted.  Blue and white bowl is 15th century, and large blue and white bowl, Swatow.  Later note:  Large blue and white dish with flaring rim and exterior fluting.  Body is grey to brown stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, crackled, green, grey shows through some of crackles, perforated.  Blue is pale blue to black.  Interior design on rim has double ring, enclosed in a foliage border.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain, unknown.  Base fragment, sherds, deep blue, and greenish white plate (?), uncrackled.  Later note:  Large blue and white plate.  Body is fine white stoneware. Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain box.  Base fragment, sherds, small blue and white vase, with simple blue panels and spirals at base.  Matt, crackled.

Glaze is glassy, finely crackled, greyish white.  Blue is dark to light greyish blue.  Interior design is sun and cloud and bamboo in bottom (probably had phoenix), enclosed by a double ring, rim has cartouches with rosettes, enclosed by fish-scale diaper pattern.  Exterior design is single ring below rim, one on lower wall.
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Base fragment, sherds, pale blue and grey white crackled, glassy, big plate, floral design.  Swatow-type.

Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Fragment, sherds, dark blue and greenish white, glassy, heavily cracked shallow bowl, with medallion and horizontal line design as found in Penon de Coron.  Swatow-type.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Fragment, sherds, blue and white, glassy cracked shallow bowl, same design as B4-104.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Complete, small blue and white bowl, with crude floral design on exterior.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Swatow-type.  Later note:  Footring rather high, inner side slants to flat edge, outer side is straight, chattermarks and a knob are present, base and inner side of footring unglazed, base is a pale salmon color.  Body is thin, hard, white porcelain.  Glaze is opaque, glassy, blue-green.  Blue is greyish, black where thick.  Interior design includes unglazed ring in bottom, encircled by a single ring, single ring on rim.  Exterior design includes a single ring on rim, halves of 2 chrysanthemums with stems and leaves on wall, also curved leaves.  Single ring near base.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Fragment, sherds, large, heavy, grey blue and greenish white plate.  Glassy, crackled glaze.  Floral design.  Swatow-type.  Later note:  Base sherd of large blue and white dish, glazed except for edge of footring, which is low and small, both walls curving in slightly to flattened rim.  The footring is sandy.  The body is thick, hard, coarse yellowish stoneware.  The glaze is thick, glassy, crazed, and the "white' is quite green.  The design was floral in the bottom and on inside walls, with a circle of spirals around inside bottom.  The blue is very dead, pale, and washed-out.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Base fragment, pale blue and white, glassy, uncrackled large plate.  Simple floral design.  Swatow-type. Glaze is pale grey, glassy, and punctated.  Blue is pale greyish blue to navy.  Interior design on bottom has large, finely drawn chrysanthemums and fat, curled, pointed leaves, double ring encloses bottom, with a wave-pattern around this.  No exterior design remains.
Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, blue and greenish white, glassy, uncrackled bowl, with flaring lip.  Interior plain.  Bottom and exterior have wild, crude, unintelligible design.

Later note:  Medium, deep blue and white bowl with everted lip and straight rim, completely glazed except for part of base and edge of footring, which is pretty high and strong.  The outside wall of footring slants slightly inward to beveled and pointed edge.  Faint circular chattermarks.  The body is hard, greyish porcelain.  The glaze is fairly thick, glassy, and the "white" is greenish.  There is a large, slight crackle visible.  The design is a white crane (?) with blue rings standing in water and flanked by 2 plants with blade-like leaves in 2 concentric circles in the bottom.  The inside lip has dots in parentheses inside of concentric circles.  The outside walls are divided into 8 panels with a lotus bud, false godroons, and a Buddhist symbol in each.

Geographic Location: Dinago Island, E coast of Surigao
Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Unbroken, blue and white plate.  Paste not exposed, probably white porcelain.  Glossy white glaze, unevenly applied.  Has wide cracks in it, like mud flat cracks, the color of which vary from dark brown to black.  Decoration in underglaze washed out blue.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate with wide flaring, upturned rim.  Center of base unglazed.  Footring has straight outer side, inner side slants to rounded edge.  Light brick color where exposed.  Glaze is glassy, greyish white, many cracks present under glaze, irregular, not present on rim edge.  Blue is soft light blue, black where thin.  Interior design is rounded vase with 2 circular flowers and rounded, curving leaves, 3 circles on each side of vase, streamers above, enclosed by 2 rings, upper wall covered with blue, except for 4 small half-round areas near rim, containing curving lines.  No exterior design.

Geographic Location: Dinago Island, E coast of Surigao
Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Unbroken dish, same ware as c5-2.  Same shape, paste, lip, glaze.  Glaze has medium mesh crackle and is more evenly applied.  Foot partly glazed, base is unglazed.  Edge of glaze very irregular.  Unglazed portion dirty cream color, and full of small cracks.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate with flaring, upturned rim.  Base and part of footring and exterior wall unglazed, sandy.  Footring has straight outer side, inner side slants to rounded edge.  Body is tannish white stoneware where exposed.  Glaze is glassy, crackled, greyish white, perforated, missing on part of interior wall.  Blue is very grey.  Interior design is deteriorated flower in squat, oval vase design - long, curving thin leaves and square with streamers above, 2 rings around bottom, wall covered with blue, except for 4 half-circles with fan-like straight lines.

Interior design is snake dragon and rows of curving lines, enclosed by 1 wavy line and 1 ring, wall has 4 groups of short, curving, intersecting lines, 1 ring on rim.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, blue and white plate, crackled - same design as C64-3.  Blue has gone metallic black in spots.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate with flaring rim.  Base and footring sandy, straight inner side, slanting deeper outer side, wide, flat edge.  Body is grey to a light brick color.  Glaze is glassy, perforated, crackled, pale green.  Blue is medium greyish blue to black.  Interior design is tree (peony) blossom visible (probably had phoenix, etc), bottom enclosed by double ring, wide rim has diaper fish-scale pattern surrounding cartouches with rosettes.  Exterior design is single ring on middle wall.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Base sherd, blue and white plate, crackled - same design as C64-3.  Light blue which has gone metallic black in spots.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Nearly complete, 4 sherds, blue and white plate, uncrackled.  Light blue.  Crane in bottom.  Simple medallion design with three horizontal lines between each on the bowl.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, blue and white plate, uncrackled.  Same design as C64-9, with addition of Greek fret around rim on interior.  Very modern looking.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, blue and white plate, uncrackled, with same design as C64-9, with wide band around rim.  Darker blue has turned metallic black in spots.
Major base sherd, blue and white plate, uncrackled, with same design as # 9.  Blue has gone metallic black in spots.
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Major fragment, blue and cream plate, badly crackled, with same design as C64-9.  Glaze is badly off color and has large cracks like mud-cracks.  Faulty firing (?).
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, cream and black plate, (with one blue and white sherd), uncrackled.  Crane in bottom.  Medallion and scale design on all of bowl.  Later note:  Medium blue and white plate.  Base and footring sandy, partly glazed, inner side is straight, deeper outer side of footring slants to flat edge.  Body is burnt a dark brick color.  Glaze is glassy, pale green, perforated.  Blue is medium greyish blue, parts dark grey.  Interior design has phoenix in bottom, enclosed by a double ring, wall has fish-scale diaper pattern, enclosing cartouches with lotus blossoms, chrysanthemums and leaves.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large, heavy blue and white plate, uncrackled.  Crane design in bottom.  Bowl ornamented with panels.  Floral panel alternating with narrow panel with `eye' in it.

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large heavy, blue and greenish white plate, crackled, same type of deign as # 15, but with different details in the floral panels of the bowl, slightly flaring rim.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, large heavy blue and greenish white plate, crackled, same type of design as # 15, but with different details in the floral panels of the bowl.  Slightly flaring rim.

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large, heavy blue and cream plate, with slightly flaring rim.  Crane in bottom.  Floral design, unpanelled around bowl, medallion and scales on wide rim.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Rim fragment, sherds, large heavy blue and cream plate, bottom missing.  crackled, slightly flaring rim.  `Pussy willow' pattern on bowl, unpanelled.  Medallion and scales on wide rim.  Later note:  Large blue and white plate.  Body is tannish to light brick stoneware.  Glaze is semi-glassy, crackled, perforated, tannish cream color.  Blue is dark blue, a little pale greyish.  Interior design is blossoming tree on wall, fish-scale diaper pattern on rim, with cartouches and rosettes.  Exterior design is single line on wall, lower wall has long branch with small, pointed leaves.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Incomplete, sherds, blue and white plate, crude, modern, with unintelligible design in bottom.  `Surigao' plate.  Blue rim.  Later note:  Blue and white plate with slightly flaring rim, unglazed lip, and a large leaf-shaped unglazed area on the base.  Glaze is fairly thin, bluish on inside and bluish with brown discoloration on outside.  Several holes and imperfections appear inside.  Bottom decoration appears to be with 4 flowers and embellished with spots and streamers, 2 concentric rings encircle the design.  The inside wall is solid blue of spotty appearance.  The blue ran badly in one spot.  The englazed lip is brownish.  No outside decoration.  4 sun or fan decorations are faintly visible on dark blue edge.

Blue and white porcelain plate.  Sherd, part of another blue and white `Surgiao' plate, but with the white rim and sprig of blue.  Later note:  Blue and white plate.  Edge of rim and part of base are unglazed, sand adheres to footring on edge and inside area.  Glaze is thick and glassy with a bluish color.  One area which was not covered with glaze and several darks spots appear on the inside.  Outside wall is spotted.
Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, shallow glassy blue and white bowl, late stuff.  Crysanthemum in bottom, uncrackled.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, shallow, blue and white bowl, glassy, uncrackled, with brown edge on lip.  Design has no enclosing lines, and consists only of single leaf with Chinese inscription.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate.  Base and footring completely glazed, footring very sandy, inner side of footring straight, outer side slants slightly to flat edge, deep crack in glaze at edge of base.  Body is fine white stoneware.  Glaze is very glassy, a few perforations, pale green.  Blue is pale blue.  Interior design is large, stemmed, jagged leaf on left, upper right has 2 rows of characters, lower right has a box, also with characters, rim a dark brick color.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Incomplete, sherds, another plate of exactly same shape and desription as C64-23.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate.  Base and footring completely glazed, very sandy, glaze very cracked on base, deep footring has almost straight sides and a wide, flat base.  Body is tannish white stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, very perforated, pale green.  Blue is pale light blue.  Interior design is small, jagged, stemmed, leaf on left, 2 short rows of characters on upper right, 1 incised box on lower right, rim is a dark brick color.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, small blue and white bowl, crackled, glassy glaze.  Crude work.  No design on interior of bowl, but on exterior.  Bottom has blue circles.  Later note:  Base and footring unglazed, both sides slant slightly toward wide, flat edge.  Outer side is deeper than inner side of footring.  Body is thin, greyish porcelain.  Glaze is glassy, opaque, runs unevenly on exterior, greyish-green color.  Bue is greyish.  Interior design includes coin design in bottom, encircled by a ring, single ring on rim.  Exterior design includes 2 rings on upper wall enclosed by a design of scrolls and alternating half-flowers, bows scattered on rest of wall.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, large blue and white bowl, glassy, uncrackled.  Flaring rim, with design.  Flower in bottom.  Inside bowl, no design.  Outside elaborate floral design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large blue and white bowl, glossy, uncrackled.  Plant in bottom.  Four flowers on interior bowl.  Exterior has only enclosing lines.  Plain rim.  Grenish white glaze.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Nearly complete, blue and white bowl, glassy, crackled.  Flower in bottom.  Interior bowl undecorated.  Exterior bowl has elaborate floral design.  Plain rim.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, blue and white bowl, with strong brown crackle.  Same type of shape and design as C64-28, but with different elements.  Glassy glaze.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, blue and white bowl, glassy with strong brown crackle.  Flaring decorated rim.  Plant in bottom.  Interior bowl undecorated.  Exterior has band of vertical flutings.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Rim fragment, sherds, blue and white bowl, strongly crackled.  Bottom missing.  Interior bowl, crude, simple design.  Exterior bowl undecorated, except enclosing line.  Rim plain.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Incomplete, 5 sherds, pale blue and white shallow bowl, of very crude late type, widely flaring sides.  Simple design on interior.  Nothing on exterior.  White glaze is really dirty grey.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, except for nick in rim, blue and white plate, crackled, with same design as C64-9.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate.  Base and footring partly glazed, sandy, low footring has straight inner side, slanting outer side and thin to wide flat edge.  Body is burnt a light brick color where visible.  Glaze is semi-glassy, crackled, greyish-green, irregular on exterior, perforated.  Blue is pale greyish blue to blackish where thick.  Interior design is phoenix in water on bottom, tree-peony on left, bamboo on right, sun and cloud overhead, enclosed by a double ring, 3 cartouches with flowers on wall, separated by 3 sets of 3 horizontal short parallel lines.  Rim has a wide and a narrow ring.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, small crackled blue and white plate, brown edge, same design as C64-23. Japanese.  Small blue and white plate.  Base and footring completely glazed, very sandy, high footring has straight outer side, inner side slants to wide, flat edge.  Body is greyish white stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, large crackle, perforated and irregular on exterior, pale green.  Blue is medium greyish blue.  Interior design on left side of plate has long, curving, pointed leaf; right side has 2 rows of characters.  Rim is burnt a dark brick color.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, small crackled light blue and greyish white plate.  Design without enclosing lines, consisting of two wierd figures on bowl.  Blue has turned metallic black in spots.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, small uncrackled blue and greenish white plate.  Design is floral, crude, without enclosing lines.  Blue a very rich blue, almost black in spots.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate with narrow, flaring rim.  Base and footring completely glazed, sandy, footring has straight outer side, outcurving inner side and wide, flat, irregular edge.  Body is tannish white stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, plae green, a few perforations.  Blue is medium to blackish.  Interior design is of pond with 2 floral sprigs, simple flowers, rushes, and longer-stemmed buds, heavy curving line in between 2 sprigs in center.  No exterior design.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, very crude blue and white plate with unglazed ring in bottom.  Crude simple designs on bowl.  Blue lines on exterior.  Later note:  Footring is low, has bevelled and gently sloping sides.  Body is hard white stoneware.  Glaze is medium thick, bluish, glassy, crackled, and cracked.  Glazed spot in center of bottom is irregular, rough, and badly cracked.  Color of design elements very from blue through dark green to brown.  In glazed spot on bottom is a single circle, around inside walls are 4 curving, broad-lined designs.  Around rim is single line.  On outside wall is a broad line beneath the lip, double line near bottom of wall, and a single line on outside of footing, 2 vertical lines connect the 3 uppermost lines at one spot.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Major fragment, light blue and greenish white, glassy, crackled bowl, straight rim.  Floral design on exterior.  Unglazed ring in bottom. The glaze is medium thick, glassy, finely crackled and greenish and orangy in spots, unglazed base is medium orange.  The design consists of a chracter in center bottom, curved pointed leaves within 2 concentric rings outside of unglazed rin, a ring just under the rim inside, and a vine of large, curved-pointed leaves winding around the outside walls between 2 concentric rings.  The blue si rather dead and greyish.

Two concentric rings encircle the bottom where the wall begins to bend upward.  Another ring circles the wall at the point where the edge begins to flare outward.  The rim is solid blue except for 3 fan-like designs, each 1/4 of the way around the rim.  The englazed lip is brown.  There is no decoration on the outside.

Bowl stained by tuba.

Celadon glaze bowl.  Green bowl.  Whole, smooth shiny glaze.  Scrawling marks in paste on sides within.  Ring near edge.  Parallel marks outside.  As if made with tines of fork. Celadon glaze bowl.  Heavy thick green bowl.  Whole. Contained pieces of gold locket with interesting design.
Celadon glaze bowl.  Large green bowl.  Whole.  Very fine crackle.  Badly stained with tuba.

Celadon glaze dish (twin-fish).  Green saucer, unbroken except for sherd and chip missing from rim.  Has flaring rim with upturned lip.  Light grey stoneware. Saucer.  Whole.  Greyish olive green.  Part of exposed paste, bottom, outside, reddish.  Well executed leaf pattern on outside.

Celadon glaze dish.  Celadon saucer.  Edge nicked a little.  Crackle.  Rather coarse.  p.330.  Also in field catalogue: Green saucer, chipped in three places on lip, otherwise  unbroken. Celadon glaze dish.  Brown saucer, with flaring rim.  Unbroken except for one small sherd out of rim.  Buff stoneware.  Light brown glaze, fine mesh crackle. 30 sherds, green dragon jar.  27 sherds located March 15, 1946, of which 3 have been glued together.
Beautiful small, two-handled olive green jar; celadon glazed stoneware..  Whole.  It originally contained about 112 gold beads, of which a dozen remained.

Grey bowl base.  Whoel. Highly polished glaze.  Evidently had cover.

Celadon glaze bowl.  Green bowl, unbroken except for small sherd from rim.  Dark blue-grey stoneware.  Soft, olive-green glaze, with an occasional crackle line.  Occasional pinholes.  Small high foot.  Rim of foot and base unglazed, and unchanged in color.

Unglazed base brick red.  Raised line on exterior.  Sides fluted, interior concave surface opposite exterior convex surface (possible Sung?).

Celadon glaze dish.  Only two out of three pieces.  Small yellow plate, with flaring rim, nearly complete, in two pieces.  Brick red stoneware.  Badly roughened, uncrackled, mustard yellow glaze, with occasional green lights in it.  Foot and base unglazed, and brick red.  Deep incised line outlining bottom.  Ring of unglazed paste in bottom.  (This seems to be a very badly overbaked piece of green celadon ware, refer to G9-a and G9-b).

Celadon glaze bowl.  Green bowl , unbroken except for large sherd gone from rim.  Light grey stoneware.  Soft, leaf-green glaze, with brown craw-claw crackle.  Base unglazed, and unchanged in color. Nearly complete, 2 sherds, large olive green crackled plate.  A,I.2.b.2.b. Later note: mended EEM.
Incomplete, 4 sherds, chalky cream shallow bowl with raised straight line decoration on exterior, like G16-a. (A.I.l.c.2.-1)
Base of large red crockery jar with hole in bottom.

Small fish vertebrae
Whole grey bowl with unglazed ring in bottom.  B.I.3.a.2.b..  Later note : like B5-6.

Whole, small black jar, dark brown glaze mostly gone, with four horizontal loop handles I.I.4.c.2.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, large greenish grey bowl, with unglazed ring in bottom.  C.I.2.c.2.b..  Later note:  like B5-6, only larger.
Whole, shiny grey bowl, crackled with unglazed ring in bottom.  B.I.3.a.2.b..  Later note:  similar to B58-2.
White porcelain bowl.  Whole, crackled small light blue bowl, with raised pattern on interior.  Rim nicked.  D.I.2.c.2.a.

Whole (rim notched) small blue and white bowl with smoothly everted lip, glazed except for a ring in the bottom and the base and footring. The base is "red-bottomed". The footring is rather high with inside wall slanting in to flattened edge. Concentric chattermarks visible. 
 
The body is thick at the bottom but thin at the top, it is hard, greyish stoneware. The glaze is rather thin, opaque, glossy, crazed all over and is buff in color. 
 
The design consists of a flared cross in the bottom in a ring; a ring just outside of unglazed ring and one just under the lip inside; and lotus buds connected with a curved vine and leaves on the outside walls between a ring under the lip and 2 rings just before the base begins. The blue is burnt grey.
Whole (many nicks in rim) white plate
Whole, miniature cream(originally brown)vase.   K.I. 4.a.2.b. Later note, like B22-1.
Whole, grey bowl, with flaring rim, and unglazed ring in bottom-pressed in center.  B.I.3.a.2.b..
Celadon glaze bowl.  Whole, small olive green bowl, with pinholes near rim, pressed flower in centre of bottom, crackled.  C.I.2.b.2.b.  Later note: like G127-1.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, dark green bowl, crackled, with countersunk base, B.I.2.b.2.b..  Later note: G68-a without flower in bottom.
Whole, small, light brown vase.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole (small rim nick), large light green celadon plate, deep, flaring rim, uncrackled, with fluted interior bowl.  A.I.2.a.1.a.
Whole, shallow bowl, dirty green brown crackle, fluted exterior incised lines interior, with flower in centre, B.I.2.b.1.b.
Celadon glaze dish.  Complete, soft green bowl, with brown crackle, and flaring rim.  B.I.2.b.1.b.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole (perfect), large soft green celadon deep plate, with flaring rim, fluted bowl, and large lotus in bottom.  B.I.2.a.1.a.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, late,crudely, plain deep geep grey bowl with bottom unglazed.  Stamped tree on bottom interior.  B.I.3.a.2.b..  Later note:  like G137-2.
Whole, a duplicate of #1. B.I.3.a.2.b..
Whole, rim nicked, small bowl of light bluish green transparent glaze, with irregular flutings on exterior D.I. 2.b. 2.b
Whole, shallow cream saucer, crackled glaze, five stile marks in bottom.  (No design but should be classed like G71-f).
Whole, small squat jug
Whole, pottery (brownish red) jar, showing ring marks.  Is obviously not native ware.  H. 10 cm. but not vase.

Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, large, heavy varying blue and white deep bowl, with sketchy dragon in bottom.  One part of plaster rim missing.  Later note:  Base and footring very sandy, completely glazed, deep heavy footring has deeper inner side, both sides almost straight, wide flat edge.  Body is whitish grey stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, pitted, missing in part of interior bottom, quite white.  Blue is pale to medium blue.  Interior design is large dragon and voluted in bottom, enclosed by a double ring, wave pattern around this, enclosed by another ring, rim has trellis pattern of cross-hatches and dots.  Exterior design is double ring on rim, double ring near bottom.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Celadon glaze dish.  Complete, big dark green celadon plate, with flaring rim and pressed flower in centre of bottom (like G135-1).  A.I.2.a.1.a..
Celadon glaze bowl.  Whole, crackled, light green celadon very deep bowl, slightly constricted at the mouth, base unglazed.  E.I.2.a.1.a.  Later note: like B1-20.
Pieces, incomplete brass agong

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, shallow crude blue and white bowl, crackled with some of glaze worn off lip, unglazed ring in bottom.  Later note:  Glazed ending in uneven line before bottom on inside and before base on outside.  Center of bottom is glazed.  The footring is medium high with outside wall slanting slightly in to flat edge.  Concentric chattermarks show on base.  Unglazed areas dark brown.  The body is medium thick and burned dark brown.  The glaze is also burned brown and covered with fine crackle.  The design consists of 2 phoenixes stamped on either side of inside walls with 2 blossoms stamped between.  There is a circular stamped design in center of bottom.  The blue is burned dark grey.

Political Location: Barrio Quimba, Lazi, adjoining Barrio to Poo
Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, large curde blue and grey bowl, with unglazed ring in bottom (same general ware as G143-1).  Later note:  Glazed except for ring in bottom part of base and footring.  The latter is medium high, thick, with flat edge.  Outside walls slants in and inside wall also slants in to edge.  Concentric chattermarks visible on base, bottom and outside walls.  The body is probably hard greyish-white porcelain.  The glaze is fairly thick and glassy.  The "white" is really a greyish blue, shows cream-color where bubbled and on edges.  The design consists of 2 stamped phoenixes (hardly recognizable), one on each side on inside wall, and 2 blossoms also opposite each other.  The "blue" is a greyish-green.
Whole, shallow green bowl with faint incised design in interior.  Glaze rough and badly discolored.  B.I.2.c.1.a..

Blue and white porcelain vase.  Nearly complete, (lip broken and smoothed off) small blue and white vase, heavily crackled, floral design.  Later note:  Small blue and white vase, globular body, slim neck.  Base and footring completely glazed, sandy, footring has curving outer side, inner side slants to flat base.  Body is porbably grey stoneware, now a deep greyish brown.  Glaze is fairly glassy, finely crackled, brownish grey.  Blue is very dull blackish shade.  Exterior design is 3 spiral blossoms on lower wall, rest of exterior covered with leaves and intertwining branches.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Nearly complete, 3 sherds, large green bowl, with flaring rim, crackled, incised design on interior, transparent glaze.  B. I.2.b.2.b
Fragments of iron knives
Whole, (rim nicked), small yellowish green deep bowl, crackled wiht glaze very unevenly applied.  D.I.2.c.2.a.
Incomplete, 8 sherds, glassy, light green shallow plate, with incised design on interior, flaring rim with parenthesis lip.  A.I.2.a.1.b.
Whole, cream-colored bowl, apparently overburned in kiln.  No design. `Mud crackle' around foot.

Political Location: Barrio Bohetambak, Muncipality of Bululibun, Tipo-Tipo
Description: Celadon glaze dish.  Incomplete, large heavy, light green glassy uncrackled celadon with flaring rim and parenthesis lip, panelled floral design on interior and exterior.  Flower in bottom.  A.I.2.a.2.a.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological and kiln provenience information by C. Gokee, 2009

Political Location: Barrio Bohetambak, Muncipality of Bululibun, Tipo-Tipo
Description: Seven lozenge rhombus shaped beads, strung with a cotton string together with nine red roughly spherical shaped beads. Generally the two kinds of beads seem to be alternating except the last three that are the red beads which seem to be missing some lapis ones in between.
Curatorial Notes: Kept now in clear box

Description: Celadon glaze dish.  Whole (except for large piece out of rim), very large, heavy, crackled, glassy, light green celadon plate, with flaring rim and straight lip.  Scroll design in low relief on interior.  A.I.2.a.2.b.

Whole, modern, crudely decorated, blue and white bowl, with unglazed  ring in bottom, with unglazed ring in bottom.  Roughly drawn small Chinese character in bottom.  Later note:  Deep blue and white bowl with slightly flaring lip and straight rim.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Footring is high with straight sides and bevelled, unglazed edge.  Sand on footring, base is glazed.  Body is hard white stoneware.  Glaze is glassy, greenish and has many air holes.  Inside walls have faint vertical ridges.  Design inside consists of a single character off-center in the bottom.  On outside walls are 3 circular designs or characters repeated by 3 characters.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, olive brown big celadon dish, plain rim with large lotus flower in bottom.  Otherwise no design.  A.I.2.a.2.a..
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, large blue and white plate, old type, with greenish crackled glazed, and good technique.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Incomplete, 1 sherd, very large heavy green celadon type plate, with transparent glaze, and unglazed base.  Flaring rim.  A.I.2.b.1.b.
Whole, black and bluish white deep plate, with flaring rim.  Of the usual pattern, wihtout the fish in the bottom.
Incomplete, 1 sherd,  cream bowl with crackled glaze, flaring lip, no design, five stilt,marks in bottom, C.I.1.b..
Whole, heavy green deep bowl, bluish crackled glaze, celadon type matt, slightly flaring rim, incised design on interior.  C.I.2.b.1.b.
Celadon glaze dish.  Complete, matt plain uncrackled celadon deep plate, with plain thickened rim.  Only design pressed flower in intaglio in bottom.  A.I.2.a.1.a.

Political Location: Barrio Salog, Dalaguete, near barrio Obo
Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherd, blue and white plate, crackled glaze, bird in bottom.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Small, irregular old Spanish silver coin
Whole, large red nativeware bowl with high foot.  Bowl has flaring lip, without interior design.  Simple indented exterior line.  Foot elaborately ornamented with wide incided lines and holes.
Whole, brown bowl with festoon lip.  Matt uncrackled glaze.
Whole, brown bowl with festoon lip, matt, uncrackled glaze.  Interior very much worn.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, large, heavy, matt, uncrackled celadon plate, with flaring rim and upturned lip, with fluted interior bowl.  A.I.2.a.1.a.
Nearly complete, 1 sherd (piece missing out of rim) yellowish green  shallow bowl, matt crackled glaze, with flaring rim.  LAte imitation celadon.  B.I.2.b.1.b..
Whole (with badly nicked rim), late cheap blue and white shallow bowl.  Crude simple decoration.  Unglazed ring in bottom.

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, one sherd missing, large shallow blue and white bowl.  Cheap, modern, simple stuff probably Japanese.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Later note:  Large blue and white shallow bowl with slightly everted lip, glazed except for ring in bottom and edge of footring.  The footring is strong, 5-sided and not real high, with flat edge.  Concentric chattermarks visible.  Ring is red.  The body is hard, greyish and porcellaneous and medium to thin.  The glaze is thin, crackled, and the "white" is quite grey.  The design consists of 2 rows of "ladder" design stamped on inside walls under rim, a square stamp in center of bottom, and 4 blossoms stamped on outside walls.  The blue is greyish and runny.
Celadon glaze bowl.  Whole, large light green, uncrackled, glassy bowl, imitation celadon, plain interior.  Lotus petal exterior.  C.I.2.b.2.a.
Whole, very deep grey bowl
Base fragment, 1 sherd, uncrackled matt green bowl.  Heavy, with thick glaze, and base unglazed.  Type of imitation celadon ware.  A.I.2.b.1.a

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, sherds, large shallow blue and white bowl, with flaring lip.  Blue of uneven color, and turned metallic black in spots.  Simple floral design, with bird in bottom.  Later note:  Blue and white plate with flaring rim.  Completely glazed except for the flat edge of the broad, low footring.  Sand adheres to footing and base.  Body is hard, greyish stoneware.  Glaze is thin, greenish-milky, glassy, and has tiny specks over the entire surface.  Many airholes in glaze.  Blue decoration is burned black in spots.  Design consists of parrot-like bird over a sprig of 2 chrysanthemums.  Behind, before, and above the bird are tree limb or flower sprig designs and 3 little circles.  Bird is enclosed in a border with 4 spiral and curvilinear designs spaced around the band.  Side walls have four double chrysanthemums designs.  Rim has trellis design.  Outside are 4 concentric circles, 2 beneath rim, 1 at bottom of sidewall, and 1 on outside base of footring.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Gold hook and eye, large, with 3 links of chain attached
Incomplete, 2 sherds, large heavy dark green matt crackled plate with flaring rim.  Non transparent imitation celadon, with unglazed base.   A.I.2.b.1.b.
Incomplete, 2 sherds, large heavy green glassy crackled transparent glazed plate, with flaring rim and upturned lip, late imitation celadon, with unglazed base.  A.I.2.b.2.b.

Whole, large, heavy, olive green, crackled, glassy, transparent glazed plate, with flaring rim.  Glaze worn off in spots.  A.I.2.b.2.b.

Whole, (rim nicked), small, glassy, crackled dark green imitation celadon bowl, with straight rim.  Vertical incised lines on exterior.   B.I.2.b.2.b.

Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Whole, large blue and white bowl, with sharply flaring rim.  Good design, of complex floral elements.  Exterior nearly plain.  Glassy, uncrackled glaze.
Whole, small pearshaped jar, without handles.  Light brown crockery finish.  Short neck and plain rim.
Whole, small, slender, heavy, red, nativeware jar, with constricted short neck and thickened flaring rim.  No decoration.
Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, dark green(blue?) and grey, glassy, crackled large bowl, probably Japanese.  Crude with bottom unglazed.
Complete, 9 sherds, large shallow blue and white plate, with straight rim.  Complex floral (?) design.  Probably porcelain.  Late stuff, but fairly good technique.  10 sherds located June 6, 1946.
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Complete, large blue and white shallow plate, with deep blue, grotesque dragon in bottom, without enclosing lines.  Straight rim.

Description: Whole, glassy, light green, uncrackled celadon plate with straight thickened rim.  Exterior plain except for raised line below lip.  interior bowl fluted, pressed flower in bottom.  A.I.2.a.2.a.
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, late type blue and white shallow bowls, large.  Glassy, uncrackled glaze. Greyish blue crude designs on interior.  No unglazed ring.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, small plates, same type of ware as G183-1, greyish white uncrackled glaze, with greyish blue curde designs interior.  No unglazed ring.  Later note (G183-2A):  Small blue and white plate with narrow flaring rim.  Base and footring completely glazed, very sandy, footring sides slant slightly to wide, flat edge.  Body is not visible.  Glaze is glassy, greenish grey, perforated.  Blue is medium to blackish.  Interior design on bottom and wall is design of pond with sprigs growing therefrom, 2 simple, volute flowers, reeds, and 4 taller buds with fat, rounded leaves present, 1 long, curving leaf in middle.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Whole, blue and white plate with flaring rim.  Glassy uncrackled white glaze.  Rim blue with areas in white.  In bottom crude drawn landscape.  Better colors and better workmanship than G183-1.  Later note:  Sand adhering to footring and in center of base.  Glaze is heavy, fairly glassy and greenish-blue.  Bottom design shows man seated in edge of stream with clump of trees behind him, across water are large trees on tall buildings and 12 brids flying across sky.  This scene is enclosed in 2 concentric rings.  The flaring rim is dark blue except for 4 sun-and-cloud designs spaced around the edge.  The dark blue shows "crackling" effects, but the porcelain itself is not cracked.  The lip is thickened and roughly finished.  The outside design consists of four springs of wheat encircling the outside wall.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Whole, small slender jug, with two vertical loop handles.  Probably originally crackled green glaze. Now heavily coated with gilt paint.  See G116-1.  I.I.2.b.2.b.
Celadon glaze dish.  Nearly complete, large matt, uncrackled celadon plate, with straight rim.  Bowl has scroll design.  Pressed flower in bottom.  A.I.2.a.1.a.
Celadon glaze bowl.  Base fragment, glassy, crackled, light green celadon bowl.  C.I.2.b.1.b.
Simple, recent, brass candlestick

Whole, small globular, jug, with two horizontal tubular handles.  Light brown uncrackled glaze, with small spots of light grey containing dark lines.  I.I. 4.a.2.a.
Whole cover to black and white round box
Incomplete, 1 sherd, light browinsh grey bowl, with unglazed ring in bottom.  Glaze is matt, apparently deteriorated.

Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, large heavy light green, glassy, uncrackled, celadon (?) plate, with incised scroll design on bowl, and pressed flower in bottom.  Foot is only light pink-not red.  Flaring rim.  B.I.2.a.1.a.
Celadon glaze dish.  Whole, green, uncrackled matt saucer, with flaring lip.  Interior scroll design.  'Iron foot' is light pink.  A.I.2.a.1.a.
Blue and white porcelain box.  Whole, top and bottom of small blue and white round box, glossy, uncrackled white glaze, with simple light blue floral design.

Description: Incomplete, 1 sherd (neck and one handle missing), large globular jug.  Glassy, crackled, transparent green glaze with incised design on upper body.  Heavy 'tears' at glaze edge.   I.I.2.b.2.b.
Nearly complete (nicks in rim and crackled), pearshaped, dark brown vase.  Rough crockery type of glaze, somewhat deteriorated.
Whole, one small handle missing, globular small jug.  Dark green crackled glossy glaze.  Rough attempts at fluting on the body.  I.I.2.b.2.b.
Blue and white porcelain jarlet.  Whole (except for rim), small globular blue and white vase.  Glassy, crackled light grey glaze, with floral design in blue, crude.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Whole, small deep saucer, with flaring lip.  Brown, matt, uncrackled glaze.  unglazed center in bottom.  B.I.4.a.2.b.
Major fragment, 1 sherd, large heavy bluish green bowl, with flaring rim.  Glassy crackled thick transparent, glaze.   Incised design on interior, fluted exterior.
Blue and white porcelain dish.  Complete, cheap, modern, crude blue and white bowl, with thickened lip.  Unglazed ring in bottom.

Nearly complete, cheap, modern, blue and white bowl, with straight rim.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Crude simple design.  Later note:  Large blue and white shallow bowl with straight rim, glazed except for ring in bottom and whole base.  The footring is strong, fairly high with straight walls and flat edge.  Concentric chattermarks show on base.  The body is hard, dark grey and porcellaneous, of medium thickness.  The glaze is fairly thin, glassy, and the "white" is greenish grey.  The unglazed ring is brownish.  The design consists of 2 phoenixes stamped on opposite side of inside walls and stamped flowers between, 2 concentric rings in brownish green in the bottom, and 4 flowers stamped on outside walls.  The blue is greyish and greenish.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Whole, large heavy greyish green bowl with flaring rim.  Glossy, crackled, transparent glaze, with incised design in red and green.  K.II.2.a.2..a.
Blue and white porcelain jarlet.  Whole (rim nicked) small squat green vase.  Glassy crackled grey green glaze, with traces of overglaze design in red and green.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Whole, small pear-shaped brown vase
Whole, small straight sided reddish brown jar, with wide mouth, and sharp shoulder.  Upper part of body roughly fluted.  Cracked.
Whole, small black and cream bowl
Whole, cheap modern light cream bowl, without design.  Thickened lip.  C.I.1.b.  Barrio Biuanon, Inabanga, Bohol.
Celadon glaze jar.  Whole, squat light brown vase.  Glossy, uncrackled glazed.  No neck, thickened lip.  K.I.4.a.2.a.

Whole, small grey saucer.  Thin, glassy, uncrackled light grey glaze ending just below rim, and with whole bottom unglazed.  A.I.3.a.2.b..

Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Incomplete, sherds, large, heavy blue and white bowl, with flaring lip.  Complex floral design in dark blue, changeable to black, with vague edges.  Uncrackled glassy glaze.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Major fragment, large, shallow, cheap, modern blue and white bowl, with unglazed ring in bottom, and crude simple design.  Later note:  Large blue and white deep plate with straight rim, glazed except for ring in bottom and base (which has a few spots of glaze on it).  The footring is fairly high, wide, and is almost 5-sided (bevelled) with flat edge.  Concentric chattermarks visible.  Unglazed part greyish orange.  The body is hard, greyish, porcellaneous, of medium thickness.  The glaze is medium thick, glassy, and the white is bluish grey.  The design was probably stamped flowers with "ladder" leaves on inside walls.  There is a rectangle with a character (?) in it stamped in brown in the bottom.  The blue is very greyish.

Blue and white porcelain dish.  Major fragment, sherd, cheap modern blue and white shallow bowl with crude design in bad blue.  Unglazed ring in bottom.  Later note:  Large blue and white shallow bowl with everted angular lip, glazed except for ring in bottom and edge of footring, which is high and thick with nearly straight walls and nearly flat edge.  Concentric chattermarks are visible in bottom and on base.  The body is hard, medium thick greyish-white porcelain.  The glaze is thin, grey and crackled.  Unglazed ring is dark brown.  The design consists of 2 very sketchy, free and impressionistic phoenixes on opposite sides of inside walls, with a trio of spirals and some impressionistic plants in between.  Very faint inscription is in the bottom.  The "blue" is actually a greyish green.
Major fragment, 1 sherd, (rim badly broken), shallow European blue and white bowl, with short foot.
Whole, small pearshaped jar with sharp shoulder and homemade pottery cover.  Dark brown glaze, somewhat badly disintegrated.
Blue and white porcelain bowl.  Major fragment, large, modern, cheap blue and white bowl, probably Japanese.  Crude simple design, Unglazed ring in bottom.

large sherd of foot of shallow European bowl. Light brown glaze with light blue design. Ok but vessel is whole.

Blue and white porcelain plate.  Whole, 'Surigao' plates, with the weird designs-all three same as C5-4.  Later note:  Small blue and white plate.  Most of base unglazed, footring has straight outer side, inner side curves to rounded edge.  Body is dark brick color where exposed.  Glaze is glassy, pale green, missing on rim and parts of interior bottom, encrusted with dark specks on exterior.  Blue is soft light blue.  Interior design is adaptation of the dragon and zig-zag line design, where 4 lines radiate from center of curving lines, 4 streamers also come from center, enclosed by wavy line and concentric ring, wall has 4 volutes, 1 ring on rim.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Fragment, crude blue and white, similar to 'Surigao' plate with obvious dragon in bottom.  Later note:  Edge of footring is unglazed, both sides of low footring are straight, edge is wide and flat.  Body is tannish white stoneware, a light brick color on footing.  Glaze is glassy on exterior, semi-glassy on interior, pale green, perforated, irregular on exterior, light brick color shows through base and interior wall.  Blue is medium greyish blue to grey.  Interior design is stylized dragon (?) overhead, with long, pointed wings, bow-knot below with streamers, enclosed by 2 rings, 1 ring on rim.  Exterior design is 1 ring on rim, 2 bows on upper wall, 2 rings near bottom.
Curatorial Notes: Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Materials: Wood; Ivory; Leather (tanned); Metal; Bamboo; Cotton; Velvet
Description:
Display shield with small weapons and artifacts attached. 


Plaque or shield, flat with edges shaped in various ways (bottom curved, top squared off in the corners -- reminiscent of medieval heraldic shield or device), made out of wood.  The backside has two cross pieces of wood and one length of metal wire that would have been used to hang the item up.  The front side is covered with baldy faded velvet (once red, now orange).  There is ivory trim along the edges in places.  The front is totally filled with various items, all of which are miniatures.  Most (all?) have numbers written on them in small letters, perhaps identifying them.  The items include musical instruments made of wood, metal, ivory, and bamboo in the top center.  There is clothing made of cotton in the top and left right.  There is also a leather purse in the top left and a wood and leather addle in the top right.  The very center has carved wood shields with black painted geometric and abstract designs.  Down the right and left sides are various weapons -- wood spears with metal tips, swords and blades of various shapes and forms of metal with ivory handles, arrows of darts of thin wood shafts with ivory points.  The bottom center has tools with metal blades or hooks and ivory handles.  Below that is a wooden quiver with ivory tip and two wooden arrows inside and also a carved wooden item on a metal pivot that may be a cannon.  Along the verb bottom is a wooden bow with a metal string and one long wooden arrow with ivory point above the bow.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Whole, small blue and white saucer with crude grotesque floral design in bottom.  Later note:  Blue and white saucer with everted lip.  The footring is low and broad, with an unglazed edge that has been worked so that it has a sharp ridge in the center.  The glaze is thick and glassy.  Several spots on the bottom are not covered by the glaze.  The "white" is blusih to grey.  One section of the rim is roughened as if the clay were broken before the glaze was applied.  The painted design, beneath the glaze, is a floral pattern which covers the whole bottom and is contained in a double line about half-way up the inside wall.  On the outside, the lip is surrounded by a dark line and three short, heavy lines are spaced around the wall.  Two of these lines have a short curved line beneath them.  There is another dark line at the base of the footring.  On the base is a dark spot which may be a design of some sort.
Curatorial Notes: Objects bought in various Chinese stores thoughout the islands. Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

Description: Nearly whole (rim nicked) large blue and white shallow bowl with everted lip and upturned rim, completely glazed except for footing and base, which is "red-bottom". The footring is of medium height with outside wall slanting in to flat edge. The wash over the base has concentric rings in it (not chattermarks). The body is hard grey porcelain of medium thickness. The glaze is almost worn away, leaving the "white" tam. The design consists of a well executed lotus in the bottom surrounded by apue-centured leaves (Like M6-15) with scroll designs in the circle around it; stylized blossoms and scroll-lik leaves around inside walls; and fals gadrooms encasing Ju-I fungus on the outside walls.

Description: Blue and white porcelain dish.  Incomplete, one sherd missing, late blue and white cheap plate with unglazed ring in bottom.  Rectangular cross hatch design repeated six times. The blue is quite true and has some very dark places (blackish) where thick.

Description: Blue and white porcelain plate.  Whole, blue and white cheap late plate, with unglazed ring in bottom.  Rectangular cross hatch design repeated six times. Concentric chattermarks are visible on base and unglazed ring.  The body is probably greyish-white porcelain, medium thick.  The glaze is also fairly thick, glassy, and the white is greenish (it is much lighter on base and bottom).  The design consists of stamped rectangular designs and free-hand leaves on inside walls and a free-hand character in bottom.  The blue is "dead" and greyish.
Curatorial Notes: Bought in various places in Valencia, Bohol. Chronological information by Li Min, 2008.

1 Bontoc war spear, barbed head. 


Spear made of long wooden shaft which thickens at head end.  The wood may have been shellacked as it is shiny.  The end has a metal cap on it, a cylinder that fits over the wood at one end and tapers to a point at the other.  At the head end, a metal ferrule is attached to the shaft, strengthening the joint.  The metal blade has a long round tang/shaft which inserts into the wooden shaft.  The head/blade itself is roughly leaf shaped, tapering to a point and with two barbs extending down and out from the base.
Curatorial Notes: purchased in Bontoc, Mountain Province, Philippine Islands - May 20, 1926

Description:
One Bontoc wild board spear, leaf-shaped. 


One spear with long wooden shaft, which has probably been shellacked as it is glossy.  Shaft thickens slightly toward point end.  The other end is capped with a metal cone that fits over the wood and tapers to a point.  At the blade end, the shaft is wrapped with two ferrules made of woven rattan.  There are marks where a third ferrule one was.  These probably strengthen the haft of the blade.  The blade is generally leaf shaped, tapering to a point.
Curatorial Notes: Leaf head wild boar spear, Igorote. Northern Luzon; from provincial commander in Bontac, Mountain Province, May 20, 1926

Description:

Round spear shaft of polished wood.  Painted metal cap at the back end fits over the wood, set permanently in place.  Head end thinner than body for spearhead to fit onto. Metal spearhead, slender point with concave notches near base.  Point permanently fit into cylindrical attachment which then fits onto the base.  Secured with two pieces of wood.
Curatorial Notes: slender spear head, deer spear, Igorote. Northern Luzon; from provincial commander in Bontac, Mountain Province, May 20, 1926

Large white rectangular textile, hand woven. Made from 3 colors of coarse thread: dark brown, red-brown and beige. 


Mid-section patterning has large alternating bands of 3 dark brown and 4 beige. Dark brown bands are divided by two smaller bands of red-brown rimmed with beige. The long side is edged with brown-red bands. 


At either end of the textile are areas of plaid. The dark brown bands are crossed with faint beige lines and the beige areas have bands of diamond patterns created by the dark brown thread.

Small rectangular hand woven textile that is primarily navy but has alternating pink and white stripes all over it. To the right and the left equidistant from the center are two lines of an embroidered pattern. The pattern is of randomly alternating arrow-like notches of navy, pink and yellow.
Small long rectangular textile, tasseled on one side. Textile is navy with pink and yellow stripe pattern.

A large rectangular faded black textile with alternating red and white tassels on one end. There is a series of lengthwise red stripes (mostly pinstripes, but a couple with about a 2cm width). A few of the stripes are lined with white square 1 cm dots. There are some striped with a very small space between them which is filled with white 1 cm squares but most arc about 5 - 11cm apart. In four of the bigger spaces are designs consisting of white figures, white ladder shapes and white 1cm squares which form zigzag and triangular patterns.
Man's bark skirt. Many long bark strands hanging down from a waistband held together by fiber.

Small long rectangular textile with tassels on one edge. The textile is navy with pink and yellow patterning. Starting on one edge are 2 alternating stripes of pink and navy followed by a stripe of yellow, a red zigzag line and another yellow stripe. Next are three more stripes of navy, pink and yellow.

Long thin textile with tassels on the short ends. The textile is predominately navy with red, yellow and white stripes going lengthwise. On both short edges (running horizontal)  is a strip of navy and then a strip of red with a thin line of white down the center. On the inward side of the red strip is a wide stripe of navy. Following the navy strip is a wide red stripe outlined in white and two thin yellow lines. Closest to the tassels are two wide band of yellow with red dots.

Hat.  Black and tan straw with mother of pearl ear flaps. 


Small round domed hat with two dark bands for decoration.  Small wavy ornaments of mother of pearl hang from each side as "ear flaps"

Large rectangular tri-color banner.  Top is a large equilateral triangle pointed downwards with a piece of red and blue on two sides to create a rectangle.  Item is machine sown.  Written on white triangle are the words "KABINATAANG GALIWAG;" "DAYAN;" "MAGBANGON"
Long bone of a large animal carved into a tapa cloth pounder with handle. Pounder is rectangular with a grooved bottom.

A large multicolored blanket--hand woven.  The textile is of white, blue, and red thread and has a semi-complex patterning.  The pattern is as follows:  On either side of the textile, length-wise, there is a 25cm wide area of navy.  On top of the navy, in the center, is a 2cm wide red strip flanked on either side by thinner red lines.  To the right is a 2cm loosely woven stripe of white, a thin red line, a 2cm wide area of navy, and another loosely woven white line this time flanked by two red lines.  To the left of the wide red stripe are three 2cm wide white stripes and three thin red lines that alternate.  On either end of the textile, width-wise, are 30 cm wide areas of blue and white patterning.  Along the edge is a 2cm wide navy border with a red line through the middle.  Next is a series of 9 blue bands created by the repetition of a diamond pattern on a white background.  The top part of this area is a band of small diamonds, 3 wide.  The center area is just white, but has 3 long stripes of blue that extend length-wise, and are evenly spaced.  The blue stripes have white lines down their centers--which are seams.  The textile is six strips of weaving sewn length-wise together.

Rectangular cloth made from 4 strips (2 pairs--2 with a slightly prominent pink stripe and 2 with a dominant blue stripe) sewn together with zigzags of yellow and red embroidery.  Also two strips sewn on the ends with horizontal stripes and short tassels of yellow and red.  The pattern is vertical stripes of alternating pink solid and blue triangle-diamond pattern.  The patterning is white thread.  There are also tassels at 2 opposing corners of the textile.

A large plaid rectangular textile--hand woven.  The piece is actually 202cm x 334cm, but is fold and machine sewn on the open side to create a piece half its original size.  Textile has thread of white, pink, lime green, navy blue, and yellow to create the plaid.  Pink, blue, and green are the dominant colors.  Yellow and white are accents.  Made of 2 separate pieces sewn together at the center.

Large rectangular piece of cloth--could be hand woven.  Thread is particularly stiff and of many colors:  Fusia, navy blue, yellow, orange, mint green, white, and a light blue.

Long, narrow rectangular textile.  Blue background with light red and yellow designs woven into cloth. Long rectangular textile.  Dark blue background with 3 red stripes along length of cloth.  The 2 smaller stripes (1cm width) have a thin yellow strip through their centers. Description:
Ch'ing-pai pouring vessel with small curved handle and spout and lid.  
The vessel is pear shaped with round sides and a low neck which is unglazed where the lid rests. Small loops are attached to the handle and lid to connect them. It is decorated in relief with a flying phoenix on each side, above a border of foliate petal panels centered by a trefoil. A pale blue transparent glazecovers the porcelain body except for the flat base, where the paste has burnt rusty pink. 
The glaze is closer to Shu-fu than the typical Ch'ing pai which is clear transparent, pale blue and thin. See also UMMA Catalogue No. 48036.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu (The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics, Ann Arbor, 1972). Uthara. 2/7/05.

Description:
Ch'ing-pai double gourd pouring vessel with a curved plain handle.  The vessel has a lobed lid, with a central loop. It has a white porcelain body and a transparent pale blue glaze, typical of Ch'ing-pai (Ying-ch'ing) and an unglazed flat base which shows a slightly grayish white paste tinged with rusty hue. 
Other Ching-pai wares in this collection include 48082, 48083.
Curatorial Notes:
Studies have been made on new features in the shape and decoration of ceramics introduced in the Yuan period, particularly the techniques of decoration such as: relief designs, carved or molded, underglaze or in biscuit, designs trailed or beaded in white slip, spotted glaze etc.
See: Sherman E. Lee and Wai-Kam Ho, 'Chinese Art Under the Mongols: The Yuan Dynasty (1279-1368)', The Cleveland Museum of Art: Cleveland, 1968; John Ayers, "Some Characteristic Wares of the Yuan Dynasty", 'Oriental Ceramic Society Transactions', XXIX (1954-55), London, 1957, pp. 69-86; Basil Gray, "Art Under the Mongol Dynasties of China and Persia", 'Oriental Art', I (Winter, 1955), pp. 159-167.

Information obtained from Kamer Aga-Oglu, 'The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', The University of Michigan Museum of Anthropology: Ann Arbor, 1972. Uthara. 2/4/05.

Description: Ch'ing-pai flat flask ewer with flattened sides and ovoid mouth and foot, decorated in relief with 'ju-I' head motifs on each side and a double petal border on the neck. A small loop at the handle was intended to attach the lid, which is missing. The porcelain body of the vessel is covered with a transparent pale blue glaze of a faintly greenish tinge, resembling that of Shu-fu ware. The glaze stops unevenly on the exterior of its sturdy foot. This ewer has been moulded in two vertical halves and joined at the seams seen on the sides where the handle and spout are attached.

The small jar with rounded sides, low neck and foot-rim, is decorated in a purplish gray-blue under its transparent glaze. Around the neck is a band of trefoils, below which are three cloud-collar panels enclosing lotus flowers and scrolls, separated by pendants of beaded jewels. The base is unglazed, showing a white paste. 
Late 15th century.
Curatorial Notes:
Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/18/05.
Similar cloud-collar panels containing lotus or other flowers and scrolls are seen in a 'kendi' shape vessel and a ewer, assigned to the late 15th century (J. A. Pope, 'Chinese Porcelains from the Ardebil Shrine', Washington, 1956) and in a jar assigned to the 14th-early 15th century (Jan Wirgin, "Sung-Ming: Treasures from the Holger Lauritzen Collection", 'Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities Exhibition Catalogue No. 3', Stockholm, 1965).

Description: Spotted possibly Qingpai covered jar with a compact white porcelain body. The base is Grayish-white, flat and unglazed. The cover is of a mushroom shape. The jar has an opaque pale blue glaze of Shufu type which is daubed with rusty-brown blotches.
Curatorial Notes:
This jar could perhaps be classed as spotted Shu-fu, as it is thicker than Ch'ing-pai and has a distinct opaque glaze, that has a greenish tinge in its grayish, pale blue glaze.
Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu (The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics, Ann Arbor, 1972). Uthara. 2/8/05.

18th century.

Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu. {'The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1072}. Uthara. 02/11/05.

Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu (The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics, Ann Arbor, 1972). Uthara. 2/8/05.

Description:
Small porcelain cup with translucent body and a low finely trimmed foot-rim. It is glazed entirely except for a band around the central glazed part of its bottom (i.e. inside the cup). Under the glaze of the base is an illegible square seal in cobalt blue. There are fine cracks on the body and the rim is slightly chipped. Second half of the 15th century.   
Found in Lumban. 
See also UMMA Catalogue Nos. 48081, 48063.
Curatorial Notes:
Examples similar to this artifact are in the Philippine Collection of the Museum of Anthropology {See Aga-Oglu, "Ming Porcelain from Sites in the Philippines", 'Archives of the Chinese Art Society of America', XVII, 1963, figs. 12, 17, pp. 12-13}.

Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 02/11/05.

Description:
Small Ch'ing-pai dish with a slightly flaring rim and a flat base with a slightly raised edge. It has a fine white porcelain body of compact texture and a thin transparent bluish-white glaze which covers it on the inside and the xterior, where it stops in an even line at the edge of the base. The mouth rim is unglazed which indicates that the dish was fired upside down. The unglazed base and mouth-rim show a white porcelain body. On the outside of the dish is an underglaze decoration of a band of stiff petals rendered in trailed slip. 
Found in Lumban. 
See also UMMA Catalogue no. 48213.
Curatorial Notes:
The Sung Ch'ing-pai, the forerunner of the Yüan Shu-fu, was evidently made during both periods in numerous kiln centers of southern China, particularly in the provinces of Kiangsi, Fukien, Chekiang and Kuangtung. (Feng Hsien-ming, "Important Finds of Ancient Chinese Ceramics Since 11949", 'Wen Wu', 1965, No. 9}

Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 02/11/05.

Description:
Blue-and-white tea-pot shaped pouring vessel with lid and two handles, decorated with sprays of sketchy foliage.   
 
The cover that came with it does not seem to belong to it (note from Sinopoli 4/30/15: not sure why this assessment was made -- the lid seems to fit well and glaze and paste colors match) -- note in cabinet for 48017 and 48075 says "the lids do not belong to these teapots but came with them" 
 
Late 16th century.  Found in Mindoro.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu.

Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu.

Description:
This octagonal Blue and White ware box is of sturdy build and has a low foot. Its lid is decorated with a hare crouched among bushes staring at the moon, which may represent the mythical story of the moon hare.Around the side of the cover are eight panels containing four flaming pearls, two conch shells, a musical stone and a pair of horns, which represent four of the eight auspicious symbols. The side of the box shows eight alternating panels of cranes and lotuses. The decoration of the box, rendered in a purplish-blue, is in the style of the Chia Ching period (1522-1566). 
16th century.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/18/05.

Description: Olive-colored Longquan celadon jar with two handles and raised floral design.

Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu.

Description:
Small Lung-ch'üan squat celadon jar with low narrow mouth rim and flat base. It has a slightly bluish-green glaze. The exposed paste of the base is burnt light brick red. 
From Lumban diggings.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/22/05.

Description:
Chekiang celadon spouted globular jar with single handle (and lid) with fluted sides, a short spout and a small loop handle (variously described as wine ewer or tea pot). It has a glossy grayish-green glaze. The upper and lower halves of the vessels were moulded separately and joined at the middle. The lid is flat and circular with ribbing on the glazed side and a conical projection on the unglazed side. There are two small perforations on the lid and the glaze is a slightly lighter shade than that of the body.  
The edge of the spout is broken.  
From Lumban diggings.
Curatorial Notes:
Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/24/05.

note with object describes lid: Lid with two holes, gray body and glaze. This came with the double-hand fluted ewer "tea pot" in Williams Colelciton show at Rackham.  This lide does not belong to the ewer (wine ewer).

Description: Yüan type, melon-shaped globular spouted vessel with lid.  Globular vessel sits on low pedestal base and has a single handle opposite the spout.  These forms are variously referred to as "wine ewer" and "tea pot"; vesseil is unglazed just above base and on base bottom, exposing a gray past.  The lid currently on the vessel has a pale yellow paste and likely did not originally go with this vessel -- it has a glazed exterior with a loop handle, and interior plug.    From Lumban  diggings.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu. -- described as Song dynasty  by her,

Description: Small blue-and-white bowl with sketchy design outside and single leaf in center insinde.  Sits on low ring base unglazed on base bottom.  18th century.  From Lumban diggings.

Pale gray paste; base exterior unglzed

Description: Light green celadon shallow dish with a band of carved lotus petals on the outside.    Found in Lumban diggings.

Description:
Shallow Blue and White ware dish with straight rim and low foot rim. It is decorated on the inside with an allover pattern of sketchy chrysanthemum scrolls with a large rock amidst it. The exterior has a sketchy floral scroll. The transparent glaze has a greenish tone and the cobalt pigment of the decoration is of a grayish-blue colour. 
16th century.
Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/21/05.

Description: Small blue-and-white flattened jar with brown bottom and band of sketchy scroll on shoulder.   15th century.

Description: Small, plain bulbous jar with two loops at the neck. It has a flat unglazed base which shows a rusty white paste.It has an opaque pale blue glaze of the 'Shufu type.
Curatorial Notes:
See: Garner, 'Oriental Blue and White', (London, 1954), pl. 1A; Boode, "Some Remarks on Pre-Ming and Early Fifteenth Century Blue and White Chinese Porcelains", 'Oriental Ceramic Society Transactions', XXI (1945-1946), London, Pls. 1, b and c; K. Aga-Oglu, "The Relationship Between the Ying-Ch'ing, Shu-fu and early Blue and White", 'Far Eastern Ceramic Bulletin', No. 8 (December, 1949), figs. 3-6.
Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu (The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics, Ann Arbor, 1972). Uthara. 2/8/05.

Description:
Ch'ing-pai double gourd shaped pouring vessel with curved handle, and brownish-black spots on the body. It has a white porcelain body and a transparent pale blue glaze, typical of Ch'ing-pai (Ying-ch'ing) and an unglazed flat base. There is no lid. Found in Barras. 
Other Ching-pai wares in this collection include 48082, 47990.
Curatorial Notes:
Studies have been made on new features in the shape and decoration of ceramics introduced in the Yuan period, particularly the techniques of decoration such as: relief designs, carved or molded, underglaze or in biscuit, designs trailed or beaded in white slip, spotted glaze etc.
See: Sherman E. Lee and Wai-Kam Ho, 'Chinese Art Under the Mongols: The Yuan Dynasty (1279-1368)', The Cleveland Museum of Art: Cleveland, 1968; John Ayers, "Some Characteristic Wares of the Yuan Dynasty", 'Oriental Ceramic Society Transactions', XXIX (1954-55), London, 1957, pp. 69-86; Basil Gray, "Art Under the Mongol Dynasties of China and Persia", 'Oriental Art', I (Winter, 1955), pp. 159-167.

(There is something inside the vessel -- not identifiable)

Information obtained from Kamer Aga-Oglu, 'The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', The University of Michigan Museum of Anthropology: Ann Arbor, 1972.

Description: Lung-ch’üan celadon incense burner of cylindrical shape with a low foot and three legs. It is decorated on the outside with eight moulded trigrams ('pa kua'). Curatorial Notes: Description derived from the research of Kamer Aga-Oglu ('The Williams Collection of Far Eastern Ceramics', Ann Arbor, 1972}. Uthara. 03/29/05.
